key_decisions.rationale: Keeps first-person setting, enslaved girl, spirit, divination, profit, and exploitative owners.
key_decisions.before: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, a slave girl who had a spirit of divination met us. She brought her owners a great deal of profit through fortune-telling.
key_decisions.after: Once, as we were going to the place of prayer, a slave girl who had a spirit of divination met us. By fortune-telling she earned a great deal of money for her owners.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And it happened as we were going to the place of prayer, a certain slave girl having a spirit of divination met us, who was bringing her masters much profit by fortune-telling.

key_decisions.after: They brought them to the magistrates and said, “These men are Jews and are throwing our city into turmoil.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves public beating, lack of trial, citizenship, prison, secrecy, refusal, and demanded remedy.
key_decisions.before: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and threw us into prison. Now do they want to send us away secretly? Certainly not! Let them come themselves and escort us out.”
key_decisions.after: But Paul told the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and threw us into prison. Now they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! They must come themselves and escort us out.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But Paul said to them, “Having beaten us publicly without trial, men who are Romans, they threw us into prison, and now do they send us away secretly? No indeed! But let them come themselves and bring us out.”
